correctness.rationale: The connected graph inverse-trace functional is strictly convex in all independent simple-edge conductances, since its Hessian has the positive trace form and edge weights inject into Laplacian off-diagonals. Feasible minimizers exist and must spend the budget. Dihedral symmetry of the prices and graph forces the unique global minimizer into two conductance classes. Fourier eigenvalues reduce the objective to a strictly convex one-variable rational trigonometric sum. At zero shortcut weight the derivative changes sign at 4(n-2)/(n+1); at zero backbone weight for odd orders, an independently derived exact secant-power identity puts the sign change at 16/(n^2+7). The even-order zero-backbone endpoint is disconnected. This proves all equality and open regimes analytically. The standalone checker independently passes 68 direct rational matrix and Fourier tests; finite tests are corroboration, not a substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The closest same-objective source formulates the general inverse-Laplacian convex program and solves other graph families, but does not identify the priced two-hop ring phase diagram. The closest same-graph source computes fixed-unit edge resistances and recognizes parity of the deletion graph, but never optimizes independent weights under two class prices. Other searched circulant studies give fixed-graph spectral invariants. No inspected primary source or retrieved mathematical index hit supplies the two exact endpoint price thresholds as a global optimization classification. Residual risk of equivalent unindexed work and inaccessible publisher full text remains acknowledged.
residual_risks: The complete publisher-hosted text of the 2006 Zhang–Yang circulant paper was not available for full-document noncoverage assessment; its abstract was inspected and no optimization theorem is described there.

value.rationale: Network planners naturally decide whether to finance redundant second-neighbor links, and cost per unit weight can differ between near and longer links. The theorem determines all global optimum support classes under a fixed budget, not a mere plug-in Kirchhoff index value, and exhibits an order-parity difference in whether the original cycle backbone can vanish. Exact thresholds scale as \(16/n^2\) versus a limit of 4, giving a concrete and nontrivial dimension-dependent design boundary. The mixed optimum is uniquely and reproducibly characterized for all finite budgets, rather than offering a one-off numerical table.
